title: Count Good Substrings of Length Three
description:
# Count Good Substrings of Length Three

A substring is called **good** if it has length exactly `3` and all three characters are distinct.

Given a string `s`, return the number of good substrings of `s`.

Substrings are contiguous, so overlapping length-three windows are counted separately when they are both good.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s = "xyzzaz"
**Output:** 1
**Explanation:** The only good substring is `"xyz"`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** s = "aababcabc"
**Output:** 4
**Explanation:** The good substrings are `"abc"`, `"bca"`, `"cab"`, and `"abc"`.

## Constraints:

*   `0 <= s.length <= 10^5`
*   `s` contains only lowercase English letters.

solutions.name: Fixed Three-Character Comparison
solutions.description:
## Approach
Enumerate every starting index of a length-three substring. Read the three characters and compare the three pairs directly: first with second, first with third, and second with third.

## Key Insight
The window length is fixed at exactly `3`, so a general data structure is not required. Three pairwise comparisons completely decide whether the substring is good.

## Complexity Analysis
There are `n - 2` candidate windows and each takes constant work, so the time complexity is `O(n)`. Only three characters and a counter are stored, so the space complexity is `O(1)`.

solutions.name: Frequency Window With Duplicate Count
solutions.description:
## Approach
Maintain frequencies for the current sliding window of at most three characters. Track how many character kinds currently appear at least twice. A length-three window is good exactly when that duplicate-kind count is zero.

## Key Insight
This is the scalable fixed-window pattern. Adding a character can create one duplicated kind, and removing a character can eliminate one duplicated kind. The answer check then becomes constant time.

## Complexity Analysis
Each character is added once and removed once, so the time complexity is `O(n)`. The frequency array has fixed size 26, so the extra space is `O(1)`.

solutions.name: Three-Character Bitmask
solutions.description:
## Approach
For each length-three window, put its characters into a 26-bit mask. If all three characters are distinct, the mask has exactly three set bits; otherwise it has one or two set bits.

## Key Insight
A bitmask represents the set of unique characters in the window. Since the window length is fixed, `Integer.bitCount(mask) == 3` is equivalent to saying no character was repeated.

## Complexity Analysis
Each window processes exactly three characters, so the time complexity is `O(n)`. The mask and counters are constant-size values, giving `O(1)` space.

solutions.name: HashSet Window Baseline
solutions.description:
## Approach
For every length-three window, insert its characters into a `HashSet`. The substring is good when the set size is exactly three.

## Key Insight
This route follows the definition directly: distinct characters are exactly the unique members of the window. It is less compact than pairwise comparisons, but it is a clear baseline that generalizes to other fixed window sizes.

## Complexity Analysis
The set handles only three characters per window, so the total time complexity is `O(n)`. The set size is bounded by three, which is `O(1)` extra space.
